# Learning harness for Claude Code

> A free, open-source Claude Code setup for students and junior developers who want to keep learning to program. Hooks stop the AI from writing practice code, help comes in steps, and a dashboard tracks skill levels.

Built by Piet Hanegraaf, an HBO-ICT student at Christelijke Hogeschool Ede, with help from Claude (Anthropic).

The site is in English (at the root) and Dutch (under /nl/). The code is AGPL-3.0-only; texts, docs, research and data are CC BY-NC 4.0.

## Docs
- [How it works](https://piethanegraaf.github.io/how-it-works/): skill levels L0–L4, the hint ladder and the guard hook
- [Install](https://piethanegraaf.github.io/install/): set up the harness in a Claude Code project
- [Configuration and privacy](https://piethanegraaf.github.io/configuration/): settings, skill maps and what data is stored
- [Reference](https://piethanegraaf.github.io/reference/): every hook, command and file
- [Progress dashboard](https://piethanegraaf.github.io/progress-dashboard/): what the dashboard shows and how to publish your own data
- [For junior developers](https://piethanegraaf.github.io/for-juniors/): keep learning at work while the AI writes the rest
- [For educators](https://piethanegraaf.github.io/for-educators/): what the harness enforces in a course, and what it cannot
- [Claude Code learning mode vs. a learning harness](https://piethanegraaf.github.io/claude-code-learning-mode/): the Learning output style, CLAUDE.md rules and hooks compared; only hooks enforce
- [Secure coding exercises in C# and .NET](https://piethanegraaf.github.io/secure-coding-exercises/): eight free exercises mapped to the OWASP Top 10:2025, attack tests start red

## Research
- [Literature review: overview](https://piethanegraaf.github.io/research/): key findings, summary, evaluation, limitations and how to cite
- [Literature review: the evidence](https://piethanegraaf.github.io/research/literature/): learning to program with and without generative AI, with an evidence grade per study
- [The shift in skill needs](https://piethanegraaf.github.io/research/skill-shift/): jobs, the economics of hand-written code, and what to practise
- [Risks and mitigation](https://piethanegraaf.github.io/research/risks/): eighteen risks of practising with an agentic coding assistant, scored, with a mitigation plan
- [Design of the harness](https://piethanegraaf.github.io/research/design/): the design principles and the Claude Code setup that enforces them
- [Build log](https://piethanegraaf.github.io/research/build-log/): what the first sessions showed, the revisions and the change log
- [References](https://piethanegraaf.github.io/research/references/): all sources of the review, by topic
- [Research notes](https://piethanegraaf.github.io/notes/): dated evidence updates behind the review
- [The eternal-junior problem](https://piethanegraaf.github.io/notes/eternal_junior/): do juniors stay junior when an AI agent does the work?
- [Secure code for juniors](https://piethanegraaf.github.io/notes/secure_coding_juniors/): is secure coding a good first niche for juniors who work with an AI agent?
- [For researchers](https://piethanegraaf.github.io/researchers/): an invitation to test the harness in a randomized trial
- [Anthropic's study on AI and coding skills](https://piethanegraaf.github.io/ai-coding-skills-study/): what the randomized trial found (50% vs. 67%, debugging gap), what it does not show, and what to do
- [Key terms](https://piethanegraaf.github.io/key-terms/): desirable difficulties, never-skilling, the eternal-junior problem and other terms, each defined with its source

## Tools
- [C# OOP cheat sheet](https://piethanegraaf.github.io/cheatsheet/): classes, interfaces, UML class diagrams and design patterns, with example code

- [Source code](https://github.com/piethanegraaf/piethanegraaf.github.io): the harness, the site and the citation checks
- [AI statement](https://piethanegraaf.github.io/ai-statement/): what Claude helped make and what was checked by hand
